2608.23028.title: PsychJail: Exploring Psychological Jailbreaks via Multi-Turn Persuasion of LLM Policies
2608.23028.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in education, healthcare, policy advising, and other interactive settings, where users engage them as sustained social interlocutors rather than one-shot query engines. This shift makes jailbreaks a growing safety threat, yet most research emphasizes single-turn prompt optimization or iterative attack refinement, leaving psychologically grounded multi-turn vulnerabilities underexplored. We present PsychJail, a psychology-guided framework for red teaming aligned LLMs through theory-grounded, multi-turn persuasion. PsychJail maps established social-psychological persuasion techniques into a tactic-conditioned attack policy. It factorizes each attacker action into a Change-of-Meaning analysis, tactic selection, and victim-visible message, operationalizing the Persuasion Knowledge Model (PKM). The policy is refined with trajectory-level reinforcement learning using a PKM-gated reward that credits early jailbreak success only when every turn contains a well-formed Change-of-Meaning analysis. Across four aligned victim models, PsychJail achieves the highest average attack success rate (87.3%) and outperforms strong single-turn and multi-turn baselines on every model. We also measure susceptibility at the action that breaks each victim, revealing four distinct model-level fingerprints that identify which persuasion levers affect each model and how broadly. These fingerprints help explain cross-model transfer asymmetry. We interpret them as four candidate psychological profiles-rationalist, credibility-driven, narrative-monoculture, and broadly persuadable-while treating this interpretation as a conjecture requiring future validation. Our findings establish psychological jailbreaks as a distinct red-teaming frontier for increasingly interactive LLMs.
2608.23028.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地應用於教育、醫療、政策諮詢以及其他互動環境中，使用者將其視為持續的社交對話者，而非一次性查詢引擎。這一轉變使得越獄成為日益增長的安全威脅，但大多數研究強調單回合提示優化或迭代攻擊精煉，未能充分探討心理學基礎的多回合脆弱性。我們提出了PsychJail，一個以心理學為指導的框架，通過理論基礎的多回合說服來進行紅隊測試，對齊LLMs。PsychJail將已建立的社會心理學說服技術映射到戰術條件攻擊政策中。它將每個攻擊者行動分解為意義變更分析、戰術選擇和受害者可見消息，將說服知識模型（PKM）具體化。該政策通過使用PKM閘控獎勵的軌跡級強化學習進行精煉，只有當每一回合都包含良好形成的意義變更分析時，才會對早期越獄成功給予獎勵。在四個對齊的受害者模型中，PsychJail實現了最高的平均攻擊成功率（87.3%），並在每個模型上超越了強大的單回合和多回合基準。我們還測量了每個受害者被攻破時的脆弱性，揭示了四個不同的模型級指紋，這些指紋識別出哪些說服槓桿影響每個模型以及影響的廣泛程度。這些指紋有助於解釋跨模型轉移的不對稱性。我們將其解釋為四種候選心理特徵——理性主義者、以可信度驅動者、敘事單一文化和廣泛可說服者——同時將此解釋視為需要未來驗證的推測。我們的研究結果確立了心理學越獄作為對日益互動的LLMs的一個獨特紅隊測試前沿。
